text:
Predicates:
SpottedNearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Cute(x) ::: x is cute.
Turtle(x) ::: x is a turtle.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Skittish(x) ::: x is skittish.
Calm(x) ::: x is calm.
Rockie(x) ::: x is Rockie.
   
Premises:
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ Rabbit(x)) → Cute(x) ::: All rabbits that can be spotted near the campus are cute.
∃x (Turtle(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) ::: Some turtles can be spotted near the campus.
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ (Rabbit(x) ∨ Squirrel(x))) ::: The only animals that can be spotted near the campus are rabbits and squirrels.
∀x (Skittish(x) → ¬Calm(x)) ::: If something is skittish, then it is not calm.
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ Squirrel(x)) → Skittish(x) ::: All the squirrels that can be spotted near the campus are skittish.
SpottedNearCampus(Rockie) ::: Rockie can be spotted near the campus.
¬Calm(Rockie) ::: Rockie is not calm.
   
Conclusion:
¬Turtle(Rockie) ::: Rockie is not a turtle.
